compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`rebar claim` (and its library/MCP equivalents) can only claim a ticket whose current status is `open`. `claim_core` (src/rebar/_commands/txn.py, ~L449-455) reads the reduced state and hard-rejects anything else:

```python
actual_status = state.get("status", "")
if actual_status != "open":
    raise ConcurrencyMismatch(
        f'Error: cannot claim {ticket_id}: status is "{actual_status}", not "open" ...'
    )
```

## Observed impact

While closing landed work we found tickets left in `blocked` status with an assignee already set (e.g. b783, c7d5, f643, 7a03 — assignee joeoakhart@navapbc.com, status blocked). Because `claim` fast-fails on any non-`open` status, there was no supported way to (re)claim these to resume/finish work; the only remaining lever was a raw `transition`. A ticket that legitimately moved to `blocked` (including via Jira reconcile now that `blocked` is a valid live-Jira status) becomes unclaimable even by the agent that should own it.

## Expected behavior

`claim` should be able to move a ticket into `in_progress` from ANY non-terminal status (at least `open` and `blocked`; consider `idea` per ticket-model rules), setting/refreshing the assignee to `ticket.default_assignee`, rather than being hard-wired to `open` only.

Special consideration — avoid claim duplication:
- A ticket ALREADY `in_progress` and assigned to SOMEONE ELSE must still raise ConcurrencyMismatch/exit 10 (do not steal an active claim).
- A ticket already `in_progress` and assigned to the SAME caller should be an idempotent no-op (not a spurious concurrency error).
- Preserve the parent-first cascade and the atomic single-commit STATUS+EDIT invariant (I2/I8, docs/concurrency.md).

## Root cause

The status guard in `claim_core` encodes `open` as the sole claimable source status. The allowable-source set should be widened (open + blocked, and any other non-terminal claimable statuses) with in-progress ownership disambiguation, single-sourced with whatever `transition` treats as claimable.

## Notes

Out of scope for the session that discovered this. Filed for later triage.
